title.narrative: Providing emergency WASH and Protection assistance for displaced households in camp settings in Northeast Syria .

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed intervention will provide emergency WASH and protection support to improve services and meet basic needs of conflict- and displacement-affected households in camp settings in Northeast Syria. The project is designed based on NRC’s existing operational presence, needs service mapping, lessons learnt, and community relations established under past funding from GFFO, NMFA, SIDA, SDC, and BMFA to provide general protection and legal protection services to camp residents, as well as conduct multiple rounds of distributions of WASH NFIs. Across the intervention, NRC aims to reach a total of 34,404 unique individuals (18,923 female, 15,481 male) in Washokani Camp, Serekaniye Camp, Tal Samen Camp, Twahina Camp, Areesha Camp, and 21 collective centres. ltbrgtltbrgtUnder the Protection sector, NRC will implement both General Protection and Legal Assistance components to ensure a comprehensive approach to meet protection needs and improve the protective environment in camps. Under the General Protection components, NRC will provide Protection Case Management services to individuals facing or at risk of protection violations. The objective is to empower individuals to address protection risks through coordinated support across sectors. Services will include tailored case plans, advocacy, referrals, provision of material assistance or cash, and Level 3 Psychological First Aid (PSS). Additionally, NRC will conduct Protection Monitoring in the same camps to identify protection risks and violations of rights affecting populations of concern. These protection activities will be implemented in the following locations: Washokani Camp, Serekaniye Camp, Tal Samen Camp, and Twahina Camp. ltbrgtltbrgtAt the same time, under the Legal Protection component, NRC ICLA teams plan to address the severe lack of documentation in NES camps by supporting individuals in Washokani, Serekaniye, Tal Samen, and Twahina camps obtain civil and/or HLP documentation. Thereby supporting them to preserve and exercise their rights. In parallel, this enhances their capacities to prevent and/or mitigate protection risks. Legal assistance participants will be identified through ongoing legal awareness and counselling activities under other grants in the four camps. Participants who are unable to obtain their documentation due to freedom of movement restrictions, protection concerns, or economic constraints will then be provided with legal assistance ensuring their ability to access critical documentation. ltbrgtltbrgtUnder the WASH sector, NRC will respond to identified critical gaps in hygiene assistance by distributing three rounds of Hygiene NFI kits to vulnerable populations/IDPs in Washokani camp, Areesha camp, as well as one round in 21 collective centers in Hassakeh governorate. This intervention aims to address the immediate and ongoing hygiene needs of crisis-affected households, with a particular focus on preserving dignity and preventing the spread of communicable diseases. The hygiene kits' content matches the recommended WASH cluster and working group design to address the diverse needs of persons with disabilities (PWDs), the elderly, and women. By ensuring consistent access to essential hygiene items such as soap, menstrual hygiene products, laundry and cleaning detergents, baby and PWD diapers, and garbage bags. This activity will contribute to improved health outcomes, reduce the risk of waterborne and hygiene-related disease outbreaks, and support overall well-being in overcrowded and high-risk displacement settings. lt/pgt
